title: Social-Media Sentiment: Can Online Noise Predict Sunrisers Hyderabad Fan Mood?
dek: Online noise around Sunrisers Hyderabad rises and falls with results. With no social data in the warehouse, the honest place to start is the streaks that set the mood.
excerpt: Sunrisers Hyderabad have had winning and losing runs that would set any fan base's mood. Whether online sentiment predicts or merely follows those runs is untested.

sections.heading: Can Noise Predict Mood?
body: Social-media sentiment is often treated as a live reading of fan mood. The question is whether it tells a franchise anything the results do not.
The CricField warehouse holds no survey, sentiment or social-media data, so it cannot measure what fans feel. It can measure what they have watched.

sections.heading: The Streaks That Set the Mood
body: Sunrisers Hyderabad's longest winning run is {{ev:sm-bw}} matches and their longest losing run {{ev:sm-bl}}. Within seasons, they have had {{ev:sm-runs3}} losing runs of three or more matches.
The chart shows the longest winning and losing run in each season.

sections.heading: Following or Leading?
body: If sentiment simply follows streaks, it adds little to what the scorecard already says. If it moves before results do, it could flag problems early.

sections.heading: What a Sentiment Study Would Need
body: A proper test would collect posts mentioning the franchise, score them for sentiment, and line them up with the match ledger behind this article.
It would also need to separate genuine fans from bots and coordinated campaigns.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Start With the Streaks
body: Until sentiment data is joined to results, the streaks are the best available reading of what Sunrisers Hyderabad fans have lived through.
Sentiment should be tested against them before it is trusted as a signal.
